[custom-syntax-1]

This oracle does not read any price. It starts from one fxSP, the f(x) Stability Pool share, at maturity and applies a fixed 15%/yr discount, so the PT price is only a function of the time left. It reads one fxSP as one USDC.

PT Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

Fixed curve. The market's implied APY is never read. A 15%/yr discount decays to zero at maturity, so your PT price rises steadily whatever Pendle does.

Underlying Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

fxSAVE's exchange rate and fxSP's share value are never read. A fall in either does not affect your health factor; one fxSP is read as one USDC.

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

USDC is never priced. The oracle reads one fxSP as one USDC, so a USDC depeg does not affect your health factor.

Upgradability

[color:safe] Low Risk

Immutable. The liquidation threshold, the discount rate and the price source were all fixed at creation.

risks.description:
[custom-syntax-1]

This oracle reads the PT's own market price on Pendle, a 30-minute average implied APY, then cuts that price whenever srUSDat's exchange rate is below its previous high. It values your PT in USDat and reads one USDat as one USDC.

PT Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

Involves the TWAP price. The market's implied APY moves your health factor directly.

Underlying Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

USDat is never priced, so a USDat depeg does not affect your health factor. srUSDat's exchange rate matters only if it falls below its previous high, in which case the PT price is cut in the same proportion.

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

USDC is never priced. The oracle reads one USDat as one USDC, so a USDC depeg does not affect your health factor.

Upgradability

[color:danger] High Risk

The liquidation threshold cannot be changed, but the price source effectively can. One key controls a backup oracle, and four hours after pointing it somewhere new, anyone can switch the market onto it.

risks.description:
[custom-syntax-1]

This oracle prices your PT from a stopwatch, not from the market: a fixed 6% a year discount that shrinks to nothing at maturity. A backup source that reads USDe's live price stands behind it, and USDe is read as one USDC.

PT Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

Fixed curve. The market's implied APY and sUSDe's exchange rate are never read. A 6%/yr discount decays to zero at maturity, so your PT price rises steadily.

Underlying Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

A USDe depeg past 0.75% reaches your PT price in full once the backup is switched on, 16 hours after it starts. Below that it is ignored.

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

USDC is never priced. The oracle reads one USDe as one USDC, so a USDC depeg does not affect your health factor.

Upgradability

[color:warning] Medium Risk

No owner, no setter. But anyone can switch the market onto a fixed backup price 16 hours after a USDe depeg past 0.75%, and no key can re-aim that backup.

[custom-syntax-1]

This oracle does not look at the PT's market price. It applies a linear discount that decays to zero at maturity, on top of a USDG/USD feed, and pins the USDT you borrow at one dollar.

PT Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

Fixed curve. The market's implied APY is never read. A 4.17%/yr discount decays to zero at maturity, so your PT price rises steadily whatever Pendle does.

Underlying Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

A USDG depeg lowers your PT price one for one. Nothing cancels it against USDT debt.

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

A USDT depeg does not affect your health factor. USDT is pinned at one dollar by a constant.

Upgradability

[color:warning] Medium Risk

A 5-of-8 multisig can change the collateral factor and the price source in one transaction with no delay. The discount rate moves only in small steps.

[custom-syntax-1]

This oracle reads the PT's own market price on Pendle, a 30-minute average implied APY, and values one USDat at a fixed $0.945 whatever it trades at. It pins the USDC you borrow at one dollar.

PT Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

Involves the TWAP price. The market's implied APY moves your health factor directly.

Underlying Price

[color:danger] High Risk

USDat's market price is never read; a fixed $0.945 stands in for it. sUSDat's exchange rate matters only if it falls below its previous high, in which case the PT price is cut in the same proportion.

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

A USDC depeg does not affect your health factor. USDC is pinned at one dollar by a constant.

Upgradability

[color:danger] High Risk

The liquidation threshold cannot be changed, but the price source effectively can. One key controls a backup oracle, and four hours after pointing it somewhere new, anyone can switch the market onto it.

risks.description:
[custom-syntax-1]

This oracle reads the PT's own market price on Pendle, a 15-minute average implied APY, and converts it into USDC with a published sUSDD exchange rate. It reads one USDD as one USDC.

PT Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

Involves the TWAP price. The market's implied APY moves your health factor directly, under a 15%/yr compounding ceiling.

Underlying Price

[color:warning] Medium Risk

sUSDD's exchange rate matters only if it falls below its previous high, which cuts the PT price in proportion. A USDD depeg past 1% reaches your PT price in full once the backup is switched on, 30 minutes after it starts.

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

USDC is never priced. The oracle reads one USDD as one USDC, so a USDC depeg does not affect your health factor.

Upgradability

[color:warning] Medium Risk

No owner, no setter. But anyone can switch the market onto a fixed backup price 30 minutes after a USDD depeg past 1%, and no key can re-aim that backup.

[custom-syntax-1]

Borrowed Token Price

[color:safe] Low Risk

USDC is never priced. The oracle reads one USDS as one USDC, so a USDC depeg does not affect your health factor.

Upgradability

[color:warning] Medium Risk

No owner, no setter. But anyone can switch the market onto a fixed backup price 16 hours after a USDS depeg past 0.75%, and no key can re-aim that backup.
